Members of the delegation, Your Excellency, distinguished persons, we sincerely thank you for attending this dialogue. In closing, we wish to acknowledge the important progress made by Timor-Leste in strengthening the protection and promotion of children's rights. The adoption of national action plans, child protection reforms, disability inclusion initiatives, and measures to address violence against children reflect your continued commitment to children and to the Convention. These developments provide an important foundation for further progress. The committee trusts that you will continue to build on them in a way that brings tangible and sustained improvements to the daily lives of children. Looking ahead, effective co-ordination, adequate resources and regular follow-up will be important in ensuring that laws and policies achieve their intended impact in practice. Continued attention to child protection systems, family-based care, access to justice and support for children in situations of vulnerability will also be central to this next phase of implementation. Further progress in justice and child reform will also remain a very important part of this work. Reliable data, regular monitoring, effective inspections and well-resourced social welfare services will also continue to support your efforts to implement these reforms effectively. The dialogue has highlighted areas where challenges persist and where continued attention would support your way forward, including birth registration, protection from abuse, neglect, sexual abuse and exploitation, harmful practices, adolescent health and nutrition, and the standard of living of your children. We recognise the challenges that you face, including your limited resources, geographic isolation, difficult terrain, and barriers to reaching remote communities. limited awareness of some rights and services, and constraints in human resource capacity. In this context, continued cooperation with UN agencies, NGOs, humanitarian partners, civil society organizations will be for you particularly important. In moving forward, therefore, sustained engagement with children, families, communities, civil society, UN agencies and international partners can further support practical implementation and accountability. Ultimately, progress will be reflected in the extent to which every child in Timor-Leste can enjoy their rights, dignity and best interests in everyday life. We also noted the information provided on monitoring of progress in implementing the sustainable development goals through the voluntary national review reports, including the 2019 and 2023 reviews. The 2023 review, entitled People-Centred Sustainable Development: Leaving No One Behind, appears to have assessed progress, challenges and priorities in areas relative to children's rights, including health, nutrition, education, social protection and the protection of vulnerable groups. I must say that this people-centred approach is very welcome. It reinforces the understanding that sustainable national development is closely linked to the wellbeing of children. By you grounding policies in human rights standards and opening progress to international review, you demonstrate a commitment to transparency, accountability, and inclusive development. We express our confidence that these efforts will continue to contribute to a more equitable and inclusive future in which no child will be left behind. We strongly welcome your openness and honesty during this dialogue and the opportunity to reflect together on both achievements and remaining challenges. We thank the delegation for its constructive engagement and for the information that you could provide. We look forward to continuing the dialogue in a spirit of cooperation and with the shared objective of advancing the rights of all children in Timor-Leste. Last but not least, we kindly urge the delegation to observe future time limits, please. Thank you very much. Thank you.
